items.where: Standard OLS affine equivariance / GREG residual form; Mozer arXiv:2603.19160 (PPI++ = GREG); Sarndal et al. (g-weight residual technique)
items.reason: Invariance of the tuned interval to z -> a + c f + b z and dependence of coverage only on the population residual e_hat is elementary algebra (theta_hat - theta = ebar_S + lam_S(Fbar - fbar_S) is a function of e_hat_S, and s_r is the sample residual). I found no paper stating it as a coverage-reduction lemma, but it is not a result of substance.

items.where: Closest: Gleser-Hwang 1987 / Dufour 1997 (forced unboundedness with positive probability; same scale-limit logic); Potscher-Preinerstorfer arXiv:2412.17470 (leverage/design condition for size control, econometrics)
items.reason: No paper found with an impossibility theorem for regression-tuned/GREG/PPI++ intervals under SRSWOR of n of G clusters, nor the characterisation 'defeating samples are those on which z* is exactly affine in f_S' with P(C unbounded) >= P(W)-alpha. The proof template (E2 equivariance + eps->0 + pigeonhole) is the Gleser-Hwang/Dufour argument transplanted to a finite sample space, so the method is not new; the application and the f-dependent frontier are. I checked the proof sketch: for S in W, z_eps data = a_S + c_S f_S + eps x_S, E2 gives C = a_S + c_S Fbar + eps C(S,x_S), coverage needs a point at distance ~|theta*-a_S-c_S Fbar|/eps from C(S,x_S); finite sample space plus limsup P(A_k) >= limsup... gives P(unbounded) >= P(W)-alpha. Sound. Numerical recheck (my own seeded f, normal, G=24, n=8): pi(5)=0.1027668, B2=5 clusters {7,10,11,12,15}, kappa(e_hat(z*))=0.0905<0.10, theta(z*)=0.2410; exact enumeration of all 735471 samples, c=100, z*+eps*u gives coverage 0.8972332 for eps=1e-3,1e-5,1e-7 = 1-pi(5)=0.8972332 exactly. Lognormal f best kappa found 0.1256 (>0.10), normal-with-outlier 0.0866.

items.where: Nothing close found; classical asymptotic GREG validity (Sarndal-Swensson-Wretman 1989; Lee-Kim arXiv:2606.08730 SRSWOR asymptotics) and bounded-outcome nonasymptotic PPI CIs (Angelopoulos et al. 2023 App. E) are different regimes
items.reason: No finite-sample possibility theorem for tuned intervals with a finite critical constant on a max-share class K_OLS(kappa0), expressed via the largest fraction of samples on which the population residual is affine in f_S. The compactness argument is routine; I checked it: standardise e, numerator bounded because Sxx_S>0, misses at c_j->inf force s_r->0, limit point (norm 1, kappa<=kappa0, compact) is affine on a common missed set M with P(M)>alpha>=beta, contradiction. Sound.

items.where: Analogues only: Potscher-Preinerstorfer (full-leverage point blocks size control), Hansen 2026 RES (leverage-driven worst-case coverage), Chesher 1989
items.reason: (a) is a hat-matrix identity; I verified numerically for all spikes and three f (max abs error <1e-10): e = (I-H)e_g, sum e = 0, sum e^2 = 1-h_gg, so kappa = max{(1-h_gg)^2, max_j h_gj^2}/(1-h_gg). (b) follows from T1' and I found it in no source. Caveat in the statement: 'h_gg >= 1-kappa0' is NOT sufficient; one also needs max_{j!=g} h_gj^2 <= kappa0 (1-h_gg). At G=24 the minimal spike kappa is 0.759 (normal), 0.559 (lognormal), 0.523 (normal+outlier; max leverage 0.477), so no spike lies in K_OLS(0.10) for these f.

what_tuning_adds_beyond_prior_art: Nothing in the literature I could access covers regression-tuned (GREG/PPI++) intervals under SRSWOR with finite-sample coverage guarantees. The Mani et al. 'no free lunch' paper treats exact MSE of PPI++ under iid sampling, not coverage or unboundedness; Mozer shows PPI++=GREG but states no finite-sample theorem; Lee-Kim and Shirota are asymptotic. The nearest conceptual precedents are Gleser-Hwang/Dufour (valid sets must be unbounded with positive probability) and Potscher-Preinerstorfer (design leverage controls size control), in other settings. What tuning adds, and what I could not find in print: (i) the defeating-sample set is the set of samples on which z* is exactly affine in f_S (zero tuned residual variance), so the frontier depends on f through the geometry of sample lines, unlike the fixed-coefficient case; (ii) the hat-matrix max-share formula for spikes and the resulting leverage-based cheapness of attacks; (iii) the possibility/impossibility dichotomy via beta_OLS(kappa0). Novelty risk: the proof technique of T1' is the standard Gleser-Hwang/Dufour scaling argument, so claim novelty for the finite-population tuned-estimator application, not the technique. Claim (iii) numbers (0.37-0.74) were not rechecked. Conclusion is provisional because several key sources were seen only via abstracts/snippets.
